questions.q: What is the only line that differs between envs/dev/main.tf and envs/prod/main.tf in this lesson?
options: The module source path, since each environment has its own module
The backend block's key value -- network/dev.tfstate versus network/prod.tfstate
The provider block, since dev and prod use different providers
There is no difference; both files are byte-for-byte identical including the key
questions.explain: Each environment folder has its own literal backend key so dev and prod state files never collide -- that one line is the deliberate difference.

questions.q: Why can't the backend key be set dynamically, such as with terraform.workspace or a variable?
options: terraform.workspace only works inside module blocks, not backend blocks
Dynamic keys are allowed, but only for AWS S3 backends, not Azure Storage
Backend blocks don't support interpolation -- every value inside one must be a literal
Terraform doesn't allow backend blocks to specify a key at all
questions.explain: Backend configuration is evaluated before variables or workspaces exist, so every value in a backend block must be a plain literal.

questions.q: Why do dev's /20 and prod's /16 parent address spaces produce differently sized subnets even though subnet_newbits defaults to 8 in both?
options: Azure automatically resizes subnets based on the environment name
subnet_newbits is actually ignored unless explicitly overridden
/16 and /20 blocks always produce identical subnet sizes regardless of newbits
Adding the same number of bits to a smaller prefix versus a larger prefix yields a smaller versus larger resulting subnet prefix (/28 vs. /24)
questions.explain: cidrsubnet() math means the same newbits value lands on a different resulting prefix length depending on how big the parent block already is.

questions.q: What does passing -var-file="prod.tfvars" to terraform plan or apply do?
options: Only works during terraform init, not plan or apply
Supplies variable values from that named .tfvars file instead of hardcoding them or prompting for them interactively
Switches Terraform to a different backend automatically
Deletes any existing state file before planning
questions.explain: -var-file points Terraform at a file of variable values, which is exactly how the same root config produces a dev-sized or prod-sized network.

questions.q: Why did Caldwell Ridge choose directory-per-environment state over Terraform workspaces for this project?
options: To physically separate blast radius and access/approval requirements between dev and prod, which a shared workspace backend doesn't provide by default
Because the module itself technically cannot be called more than once per workspace
Because workspaces are deprecated and no longer supported in current Terraform versions
Because Terraform workspaces don't support the azurerm backend at all
questions.explain: Lesson 18's tradeoff applies here directly: separate state files give prod its own backend key and its own CI approval gate, not just a shared one everyone can apply to.
